subject: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response provenance — Synapse Labs
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@synapselabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@synapselabs.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA / no-training evidence request — Synapse Labs

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the conversation last week. Our legal and infra teams reviewed the draft DPA and they requested concrete evidence that customer prompts and responses will not be used to improve Redwood models (no-training / no-learn) for our Hosted deployment. Specifically Synapse needs:

- A short operational description of how Redwood segregates and prevents data from entering training pipelines (for Hosted customers who opt out).
- Records we can provide to auditors: sample audit logs showing retention, deletions, and any data exports.
- An explanation of what you persist (full prompt/response text vs. ephemeral KV only) and how long.
- KMS / residency commitments and whether keys or data can be exported cross-border.

We attached our standard security questionnaire for reference. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) offer a contract-level no-training commitment for Hosted customers, and (b) provide an evidence bundle (attestation + logs) we can share with our compliance team?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ruiz
Head of Platform Security, Synapse Labs
[Attachment: synapselabs_security_questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 180KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@synapselabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / no-training evidence request — Synapse Labs

Alex — thanks for the clear list, and copying our privacy/ops folks. Short answers up front: yes we can provide a contract-level "no-training" setting for Hosted customers as an addendum, and yes we will assemble an evidence bundle suitable for an auditor. A few important caveats and operational details below so your team knows what we can and cannot change for Hosted vs Private deployments.

On how it works (high level):
- No-learning opt-out is enforced at the routing layer: requests from an opt-out tenant are tagged and routed to inference paths that are excluded from model-improvement telemetry.
- We stop retention of full inputs in our training telemetry pipeline and prevent those events from entering long-term training stores. Short-lived traces (for debugging) are retained only with PII redaction and are auto-deleted per your SLO.
- Ephemeral KV (per-session) used for context caching remains ephemeral; by default it is not written to persistent training stores.

Evidence we can provide:
- An operations manifest that lists the retention policies, pipeline filters, and the flag used to mark opt-out tenants.
- Sample, redacted audit logs showing a request lifecycle (ingest -> inference -> deletion/expiry) for an opt-out tenant.
- A signed attestation from our Privacy Ops lead confirming the opt-out has been applied and the steps taken.
- Architecture diagram showing how we isolate telemetry and the storage buckets/queues used for no-train traffic.

Items we will double-check with infra/legal: whether we can provide raw unredacted logs for auditor review (programmatic export via SFTP/secure bucket) versus a redacted sample. We can also offer an onshore KMS binding for customer-managed keys for higher assurance.

Next steps I propose:
1) We assemble a 10-15 page evidence manifest and two redacted log samples (ETA 7 business days).
2) Follow-up call to walk the Synapse compliance team through the artifacts and pipeline filters (30–45 minutes).
3) DPA amendment with the explicit no-training clause and attestation language (we'll draft).

Attaching our standard evidence manifest template so you can confirm the fields.

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_evidence_manifest.pdf (pdf, 240KB)]

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@synapselabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@synapselabs.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / no-training evidence request — Synapse Labs

Thanks — helpful. A couple clarifying points from our infra/infosec teams:

- Synapse will be using the Hosted API (not Dedicated or Private) initially. We need assurance that Hosted customers can get the same operational isolation as Private customers when they sign the no-training addendum. In other words, we can't be told "move to Private" as the only way to get evidence.
- We also need to understand token-level retention: do you ever persist raw prompts/LLM outputs in cold storage for debugging or rollback, even if flagged as opt-out?
- Our legal team is also asking for fallback behavior — if a no-train tenant hits an unexpected error and falls back to a different model variant, what guarantees exist that the fallback traffic won't be ingested into training telemetry?

We prefer an SFTP export of redacted logs plus a signed attestation. Can you confirm whether Redwood legal would accept our suggested attestation wording (I can share it) or if you'd propose your standard attestation language?

—Alex

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@synapselabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / no-training evidence request — Synapse Labs

Alex — good questions, answered inline.

- Hosted parity: we can implement the no-train opt-out for Hosted customers without requiring migration to Private. The primary differences are operational: Hosted opt-out is enforced by tenant flags and pipeline filters; Private gives network isolation and customer-managed keys. We will provide the same evidence bundle for Hosted opt-out customers.

- Token retention: for opt-out tenants we configure the telemetry pipeline to stop persisting raw prompt/response bodies in long-term training stores. Short-term diagnostics traces may exist in ephemeral debugging logs for up to 72 hours by default; those traces are redacted for PII and can be set to 0 hours on request.

- Fallbacks: traffic routed to fallback model variants is still tagged with the opt-out tenant flag. Our routing layer blocks telemetry sink subscriptions for any request with the opt-out tag. We will include a sample trace that demonstrates the flag propagation through routing and fallback logic.

Export & attestation options:
- We can provide an SFTP drop with redacted sample logs or a secure, time-limited signed URL for auditor download.
- We will propose Redwood's attestation language; happy to receive Synapse's draft and reconcile quickly.

Timeline: if we have your confirmation to proceed, we can produce the evidence manifest + two redacted trace samples and an initial attestation draft in 7 business days. If Synapse needs unredacted logs for a third-party auditor on a specific NDA, we'll run a narrow process (legal review + tightly-scoped SFTP access).

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wednesday 5/5 to walk infra through the log samples and confirm the attestation wording. Does 10:00am PT work?

Best,
Soojin
[Attachment: runbook_no_train_steps.md (text, 6KB)]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@synapselabs.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / no-training evidence request — Synapse Labs

Alex — David here (Privacy Ops). A couple pragmatic notes for your auditors and our teams so the evidence packet is actionable:

- We'll include: (1) a compact architecture diagram; (2) the retention policy excerpt with exact storage locations and TTLs; (3) two sample traces one for a normal inference and one for a fallback path showing the opt-out tenant flag; and (4) the signed attestation.
- If Synapse needs to validate keys/crypto residency we can do a binding exercise with an onshore KMS; we'll outline the work effort in the manifest.
- For procurement/legal: we'll add narrowly-scoped language to the DPA amendment that requires Redwood to provide the evidence bundle within X business days after request and to maintain the opt-out flag semantics; however, we will not accept language that indemnifies against downstream misuse of Synapse-provided data beyond Redwood's control.

I'll prepare the draft attestation and evidence manifest template for your review. Call confirmed for Wed 2027-05-05 10:00am PT unless you ask to reschedule.

-David
David Kim
Head of Privacy Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: privacy_op_attestation_draft.docx (docx, 28KB)]
